paragraphs.title: Entering the Land and Its Inhabitants

easy.question: Who will bring the Israelites into the land?
answers: The Lord your God
The king of Egypt
The seven nations
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord thy God shall bring thee into the land.”

easy.question: How many nations are mentioned in the verse?
answers: Five
Seven
Ten
easy.explanation: The verse ends by mentioning “seven nations.”

easy.question: How are the nations in the land described?
answers: Few and weak
Distant and unknown
More numerous and mightier than Israel
easy.explanation: The verse describes them as “seven nations greater and mightier than thou.”

medium.question: What does “to possess it” mean in the phrase “the land whither thou goest to possess it”?
answers: To take possession of it and live in it
To leave it immediately
To see it from a distance
medium.explanation: In context, Israel is going to the land in order to take possession of it.

medium.question: What will happen to the nations when Israel arrives in the land?
answers: They will invite Israel to a feast
They will be driven out before Israel
They will become kings of Israel
medium.explanation: The Lord will cast the nations out before Israel.

medium.question: Why does the verse emphasize that the nations are more numerous and mightier than Israel?
answers: To say that Israel will not enter the land
To show that the nations rightly own the land
To emphasize that the Lord will help Israel against a strong enemy
medium.explanation: The comparison shows that Israel’s success depends on the Lord’s help.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “before thee” about Israel’s role in the event?
answers: The nations will retreat before Israel
Israel will remain outside the land
Israel must flee from the nations
challenge.explanation: The nations are cast out before Israel as Israel enters the land.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that these are different nations rather than one nation?
answers: The word “land”
The list of seven nations
The phrase “thy God”
challenge.explanation: The verse lists seven different peoples by name.

challenge.question: What is the order of events described in the verse?
answers: Israel possesses the land, and then the Lord brings them there
The nations grow stronger, and then Israel leaves
The Lord brings Israel into the land, and then casts out the nations before them
challenge.explanation: First the Lord brings Israel into the land; then He casts out the nations before them.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “before thee” about Israel’s role in the event?
answers: The nations will retreat before Israel
Israel will remain outside the land
Israel must flee from the nations
questions.explanation: The nations are cast out before Israel as Israel enters the land.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that these are different nations rather than one nation?
answers: The word “land”
The list of seven nations
The phrase “thy God”
questions.explanation: The verse lists seven different peoples by name.

questions.question: What is the order of events described in the verse?
answers: Israel possesses the land, and then the Lord brings them there
The nations grow stronger, and then Israel leaves
The Lord brings Israel into the land, and then casts out the nations before them
questions.explanation: First the Lord brings Israel into the land; then He casts out the nations before them.

easy.question: Who gives the nations over to Israel?
answers: The Lord your God
The king of Israel
The people themselves
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord thy God shall deliver them before thee.”

easy.question: What relationship are the Israelites forbidden to form with the nations?
answers: Trade relationships
Intermarriage
Neighborly relationships
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them.”

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to do with the nations’ graven images?
answers: Keep them
Decorate them
Burn them with fire
easy.explanation: The verse says to burn their graven images with fire.

medium.question: What may happen if the Israelites marry people from the nations?
answers: Their children may serve other gods
The nations will help Israel
Israel will receive more land
medium.explanation: The passage warns that such marriages may turn Israel’s children away to serve other gods.

medium.question: What does “utterly destroy them” mean in this passage?
answers: Invite them to a feast
Destroy them completely
Forgive them immediately
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means to destroy them completely.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites forbidden to marry people from the nations?
answers: Because the nations were geographically distant
Because they had no families
Because this could turn Israel away from serving the Lord
medium.explanation: The passage says they might turn Israel’s children away to serve other gods.

challenge.question: What is the main connection between forbidding covenants, forbidding intermarriage, and destroying the altars?
answers: All were intended to prevent the nations’ religious influence on Israel
All were intended to encourage trade with the nations
All were intended to preserve the nations’ customs
challenge.explanation: These commands prevent relationships and influences that could lead Israel to serve other gods.

challenge.question: What does the wording “Thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son” show?
answers: Only Israelite women were forbidden to marry foreigners
The prohibition applied in both directions
Only the sons of kings were forbidden to marry
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids both giving an Israelite daughter to a foreign son and taking a foreign daughter for an Israelite son.

challenge.question: What sequence of actions is given in verse 5 concerning idolatry?
answers: Burn the images, cut down the groves, break the images, and destroy the altars
Break the images, burn the images, destroy the altars, and cut down the groves
Destroy the altars, break the images, cut down the groves, and burn the graven images
challenge.explanation: The verse lists the actions in this order: destroy the altars, break the images, cut down the groves, and burn the graven images.

questions.question: What is the main connection between forbidding covenants, forbidding intermarriage, and destroying the altars?
answers: All were intended to prevent the nations’ religious influence on Israel
All were intended to encourage trade with the nations
All were intended to preserve the nations’ customs
questions.explanation: These commands prevent relationships and influences that could lead Israel to serve other gods.

questions.question: What does the wording “Thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son” show?
answers: Only Israelite women were forbidden to marry foreigners
The prohibition applied in both directions
Only the sons of kings were forbidden to marry
questions.explanation: The verse forbids both giving an Israelite daughter to a foreign son and taking a foreign daughter for an Israelite son.

questions.question: What sequence of actions is given in verse 5 concerning idolatry?
answers: Burn the images, cut down the groves, break the images, and destroy the altars
Break the images, burn the images, destroy the altars, and cut down the groves
Destroy the altars, break the images, cut down the groves, and burn the graven images
questions.explanation: The verse lists the actions in this order: destroy the altars, break the images, cut down the groves, and burn the graven images.

paragraphs.title: A Holy People Chosen in Love and Covenant

easy.question: Who chose Israel to be His special people?
answers: The Lord their God
Pharaoh, king of Egypt
All the nations
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord chose Israel to be His special people.

easy.question: What does the passage say about Israel’s size compared with other peoples?
answers: They were the largest people
They were the fewest of all peoples
They were equal to all other peoples
easy.explanation: The passage says Israel was the fewest of all peoples.

easy.question: From what did the Lord redeem Israel?
answers: From the land of Canaan
From the royal palace
From the house of bondage in Egypt
easy.explanation: The Lord redeemed Israel from the house of bondmen and from Pharaoh.

medium.question: Why did the Lord choose Israel even though they were few?
answers: Because He loved them and kept His oath to their fathers
Because they were the largest people
Because they had defeated every nation
medium.explanation: The passage explains the choice through the Lord’s love and His faithfulness to His oath to their fathers.

medium.question: What does “a special people” mean in this passage?
answers: A people in danger
A treasured and distinct people belonging to the Lord
A people living in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes a people specially valued by and belonging to the Lord.

medium.question: What does the passage promise about the Lord toward those who love Him and keep His commandments?
answers: They will never face difficulties
They will become larger than every nation
He will keep covenant and mercy with them for a thousand generations
medium.explanation: The Lord is described as keeping covenant and mercy with those who love Him and keep His commandments.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears between the Lord’s treatment of those who love Him and those who hate Him?
answers: He keeps covenant and mercy with those who love Him, but repays those who hate Him promptly
Those who love Him are punished, while those who hate Him are rewarded
The passage makes no distinction
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts enduring mercy for those who love the Lord with direct repayment for those who hate Him.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “to his face” emphasize in verse 10?
answers: The one who hates the Lord will be punished only after a thousand generations
The repayment is not delayed but comes directly to the one who hates Him
The one who hates the Lord can hide from punishment
challenge.explanation: The phrase, together with “he will not be slack,” emphasizes immediate and direct repayment.

challenge.question: What conclusion follows from Israel being “the fewest of all people” and yet being chosen?
answers: The choice resulted from great military strength
The choice depended on their large population
The choice came from the Lord’s love and faithfulness to their fathers, not from Israel’s size
challenge.explanation: The passage rules out population size as the reason for Israel’s election.

questions.question: What central contrast appears between the Lord’s treatment of those who love Him and those who hate Him?
answers: He keeps covenant and mercy with those who love Him, but repays those who hate Him promptly
Those who love Him are punished, while those who hate Him are rewarded
The passage makes no distinction
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts enduring mercy for those who love the Lord with direct repayment for those who hate Him.

questions.question: What does the phrase “to his face” emphasize in verse 10?
answers: The one who hates the Lord will be punished only after a thousand generations
The repayment is not delayed but comes directly to the one who hates Him
The one who hates the Lord can hide from punishment
questions.explanation: The phrase, together with “he will not be slack,” emphasizes immediate and direct repayment.

questions.question: What conclusion follows from Israel being “the fewest of all people” and yet being chosen?
answers: The choice resulted from great military strength
The choice depended on their large population
The choice came from the Lord’s love and faithfulness to their fathers, not from Israel’s size
questions.explanation: The passage rules out population size as the reason for Israel’s election.

paragraphs.title: Keeping the Commandments and the Blessing of the Land

easy.question: What does Moses command Israel to do in verse 11?
answers: Keep the commandments, statutes, and judgments
Build new cities
Leave the land of Israel
easy.explanation: Verse 11 commands Israel to keep and do the commandments, statutes, and judgments.

easy.question: What does the Lord promise Israel if they keep His judgments?
answers: They will not have to work
Love, blessing, and multiplication
They will return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage promises that the Lord will love, bless, and multiply Israel.

easy.question: What does the Lord warn Israel against in verse 16?
answers: Growing crops
Eating fruit
Serving the gods of the nations
easy.explanation: The verse warns Israel not to serve the gods of the nations, because that would be a snare.

medium.question: What condition is mentioned before the Lord keeps His covenant and mercy with Israel?
answers: They must listen to, keep, and do His judgments
They must conquer many lands
They must build temples for other nations
medium.explanation: The passage connects hearing and doing the judgments with the Lord’s keeping His covenant and mercy.

medium.question: What does “barren” mean in the phrase “there shall not be male or female barren among you”?
answers: A sick person
A person or animal unable to have offspring
A person who does not work
medium.explanation: The verse contrasts barrenness with the blessing of fruitfulness among people and cattle.

medium.question: What promise follows the promise of blessing the crops and animals?
answers: A promise to return to Egypt
A promise that no nations would remain in the land
A promise that sickness would be removed
medium.explanation: After promising blessing for the land, cattle, and flocks, the Lord promises to take away sickness.

challenge.question: Why must Israel neither pity the nations nor serve their gods?
answers: Because serving their gods would be a snare to Israel
Because the nations did not know how to cultivate their land
Because Israel could not understand their language
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that serving the gods of the nations would be a snare.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “the evil diseases of Egypt” indicate about Israel’s experience?
answers: They had never heard of disease
They had known the severe diseases associated with Egypt
They wanted to return and live in Egypt
challenge.explanation: The verse refers to diseases of Egypt that Israel knew and promises they would not be placed upon Israel.

challenge.question: According to the order in verse 12, what is required before the promise that the covenant will be kept?
answers: Only hearing the judgments
Only keeping the judgments in one’s heart
Hearing, keeping, and doing the judgments
challenge.explanation: The verse presents a sequence of hearing, keeping, and doing before the promise of covenant mercy.

questions.question: Why must Israel neither pity the nations nor serve their gods?
answers: Because serving their gods would be a snare to Israel
Because the nations did not know how to cultivate their land
Because Israel could not understand their language
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that serving the gods of the nations would be a snare.

questions.question: What does the phrase “the evil diseases of Egypt” indicate about Israel’s experience?
answers: They had never heard of disease
They had known the severe diseases associated with Egypt
They wanted to return and live in Egypt
questions.explanation: The verse refers to diseases of Egypt that Israel knew and promises they would not be placed upon Israel.

questions.question: According to the order in verse 12, what is required before the promise that the covenant will be kept?
answers: Only hearing the judgments
Only keeping the judgments in one’s heart
Hearing, keeping, and doing the judgments
questions.explanation: The verse presents a sequence of hearing, keeping, and doing before the promise of covenant mercy.

paragraphs.title: Remembering the Exodus and Overcoming Fear

easy.question: What concern might Israel have in their heart according to verse 17?
answers: That the nations are more numerous and stronger
That there will be no food
That they will lose their way
easy.explanation: Israel may ask how they can dispossess nations that are more numerous than they are.

easy.question: Whom are the Israelites commanded not to fear?
answers: Egypt alone
The nations they fear
Moses
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt not be afraid of them.”

easy.question: What will the Lord send among the nations according to verse 20?
answers: Angels
Rain
The hornet
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord will send the hornet among them.

medium.question: Why must Israel remember what the Lord did to Pharaoh and Egypt?
answers: To gain courage and not fear the nations
To return to Egypt
To learn the Egyptian language
medium.explanation: The Exodus shows that the Lord can save Israel from powerful enemies, so Israel need not fear.

medium.question: What does “dispossess them” mean in “How can I dispossess them?”
answers: Take money from them
Drive them out and take possession of their land
Learn from them
medium.explanation: In context, it means driving the nations out and taking possession of their place.

medium.question: What is the main sequence of events in these verses?
answers: Israel fears, returns to Egypt, and then sees the plagues
The hornet comes, and then Israel remembers Pharaoh
Israel remembers the Exodus, gains courage, and the Lord helps them against the nations
medium.explanation: The passage moves from fear to remembering the Exodus and then to the promise of the Lord’s help.

challenge.question: What is the connection between the concern in verse 17 and the command “Thou shalt not be afraid” in verse 18?
answers: Remembering the miracles in Egypt answers Israel’s fear of the nations
The concern proves that Israel must flee
The command removes the need to remember the Exodus
challenge.explanation: The memory of the Lord’s power in Egypt is presented as the answer to Israel’s fear.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “those that are left, and hide themselves from thee” emphasize?
answers: Only the leaders will be punished
Even those who remain or hide will not escape
The nations will willingly hide among the Israelites
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord’s action will reach even enemies who remain or try to hide.

challenge.question: What does verse 20 add to the Lord’s action described in verse 19?
answers: The Lord will help Israel only through a large army
The nations will surrender without any action by the Lord
The Lord will also send the hornet to destroy those who remain or hide
challenge.explanation: Verse 20 adds the hornet as another means by which the remaining enemies will be destroyed.

questions.question: What is the connection between the concern in verse 17 and the command “Thou shalt not be afraid” in verse 18?
answers: Remembering the miracles in Egypt answers Israel’s fear of the nations
The concern proves that Israel must flee
The command removes the need to remember the Exodus
questions.explanation: The memory of the Lord’s power in Egypt is presented as the answer to Israel’s fear.

questions.question: What does the phrase “those that are left, and hide themselves from thee” emphasize?
answers: Only the leaders will be punished
Even those who remain or hide will not escape
The nations will willingly hide among the Israelites
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes that the Lord’s action will reach even enemies who remain or try to hide.

questions.question: What does verse 20 add to the Lord’s action described in verse 19?
answers: The Lord will help Israel only through a large army
The nations will surrender without any action by the Lord
The Lord will also send the hornet to destroy those who remain or hide
questions.explanation: Verse 20 adds the hornet as another means by which the remaining enemies will be destroyed.

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Presence and Gradual Victory

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded not to fear?
answers: The nations
The wild animals
The kings
easy.explanation: The passage says not to be afraid of the nations.

easy.question: Who is among Israel according to the passage?
answers: The king of Israel
The Lord your God
A large army
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord thy God is among you.”

easy.question: What will happen to the kings of the nations?
answers: They will flee into the wilderness
They will surrender willingly
They will be delivered into Israel’s hand
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Lord will deliver their kings into Israel’s hand.

medium.question: Why will the nations be driven out “by little and little” rather than all at once?
answers: So that the wild animals do not multiply in the land
Because Israel did not want to fight
Because the kings asked for more time
medium.explanation: The verse says that driving them out quickly would allow the wild animals to increase.

medium.question: What does “put out those nations before thee” mean?
answers: The Lord will bless the nations
The Lord will remove and drive out the nations
The Lord will hide the nations
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord will drive the nations out from before Israel.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: The nations are delivered, then Israel becomes afraid, and then they multiply
Israel immediately destroys all the nations, and then the Lord helps them
The Lord drives out the nations gradually, delivers them to Israel, and Israel destroys them
medium.explanation: The Lord first drives them out gradually, then delivers them into Israel’s hand, and Israel destroys them.

challenge.question: What idea shared by verses 21 and 23 explains why Israel need not fear?
answers: The great and terrible Lord is among them and acts for them
The nations have no kings or armies
Israel is naturally stronger
challenge.explanation: The Lord is among Israel and brings confusion upon their enemies, so their confidence comes from Him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “there shall no man be able to stand before thee”?
answers: No one will be able to stand against Israel
Everyone will leave the land willingly
Israel will not need to travel through the land
challenge.explanation: To stand before someone here means to oppose them; no enemy will be able to resist Israel.

challenge.question: What important detail is easy to miss in the description of victory over the nations?
answers: The victory occurs without any action by the Lord
The Lord delivers the kings into Israel’s hand, but Israel loses their name
The victory is described as gradual rather than as an immediate destruction of everyone
challenge.explanation: The nations are driven out little by little so that the wild animals will not multiply.

questions.question: What idea shared by verses 21 and 23 explains why Israel need not fear?
answers: The great and terrible Lord is among them and acts for them
The nations have no kings or armies
Israel is naturally stronger
questions.explanation: The Lord is among Israel and brings confusion upon their enemies, so their confidence comes from Him.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “there shall no man be able to stand before thee”?
answers: No one will be able to stand against Israel
Everyone will leave the land willingly
Israel will not need to travel through the land
questions.explanation: To stand before someone here means to oppose them; no enemy will be able to resist Israel.

questions.question: What important detail is easy to miss in the description of victory over the nations?
answers: The victory occurs without any action by the Lord
The Lord delivers the kings into Israel’s hand, but Israel loses their name
The victory is described as gradual rather than as an immediate destruction of everyone
questions.explanation: The nations are driven out little by little so that the wild animals will not multiply.

easy.question: What are the Israelites commanded to do with the graven images?
answers: Burn them with fire
Decorate their houses with them
Keep them in a safe
easy.explanation: The verse commands Israel to burn the graven images with fire.

easy.question: What must they not desire on the graven images?
answers: The wood and stone
The silver and gold on them
The house where they are found
easy.explanation: The verse says not to desire or take the silver and gold on them.

easy.question: What might happen if someone takes the silver and gold from an image?
answers: He will become rich immediately
He will be able to sell it
He may be trapped or ensnared by it
easy.explanation: The verse warns that a person may be ensnared by taking the precious metals.

medium.question: Why must the silver and gold on the images not be taken?
answers: They could cause a person to stumble and become ensnared
The silver does not belong to the person
Gold cannot be used
medium.explanation: The stated reason is that taking them could become a snare.

medium.question: What does “abomination” mean in this passage?
answers: Something valuable
Something detestable and forbidden
Something ancient
medium.explanation: The context presents the idol as something detestable that must be rejected and destroyed.

medium.question: What sequence of actions emerges from these verses?
answers: Take the gold, sell it, and then burn the image
Bring the image home, hide it, and protect it
Burn the image, do not take its wealth, and do not bring an abomination into the house
medium.explanation: The verses command the images to be burned, forbid taking their silver and gold, and forbid bringing an abomination into the house.

challenge.question: What does the prohibition against both the image and its silver and gold teach?
answers: Even a valuable object connected with idolatry can draw a person toward what is forbidden
Only silver and gold matter in serving the Lord
The image itself is not forbidden
challenge.explanation: The metals are also forbidden so that their value will not attract anyone to an object connected with idolatry.

challenge.question: What does “a cursed thing like it” mean if someone brings the abomination into the house?
answers: The person will receive the abomination as a gift
The person will come under the same curse or ban as the abomination
The person will be able to purify the abomination at home
challenge.explanation: The verse compares the person with the forbidden object and warns that bringing it inside brings the same judgment.

challenge.question: What does the repeated wording “utterly detest it, and utterly abhor it” emphasize?
answers: That the image may be used a little
That it is uncertain whether the image is forbidden
Complete and emphatic rejection of the abomination
challenge.explanation: The repetition strongly emphasizes that the abomination must be rejected completely.

questions.question: What does the prohibition against both the image and its silver and gold teach?
answers: Even a valuable object connected with idolatry can draw a person toward what is forbidden
Only silver and gold matter in serving the Lord
The image itself is not forbidden
questions.explanation: The metals are also forbidden so that their value will not attract anyone to an object connected with idolatry.

The person will be able to purify the abomination at home
questions.explanation: The verse compares the person with the forbidden object and warns that bringing it inside brings the same judgment.

answers: That the image may be used a little
That it is uncertain whether the image is forbidden
Complete and emphatic rejection of the abomination
questions.explanation: The repetition strongly emphasizes that the abomination must be rejected completely.
